gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 explicitly identifies the same Black--Scholes example, the same claimed uniform-ellipticity assumptions, and the same failure at x=0 caused by the diagonal coefficient matrix being singular. It therefore directly diagnoses why the example is not covered by the assumption-dependent theory.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries identify the false verification that the geometric Brownian-motion coefficient sigma(s,x)=sigma diag(x^1,...,x^d) is uniformly elliptic on all of R^d; at a zero coordinate its covariance cannot dominate kappa|xi|^2 for any positive kappa.

component_coverage.gold_component: The Black--Scholes example is incorrectly claimed to satisfy the global uniform-ellipticity assumptions, although its covariance is degenerate at x=0 and thus the example is not covered by the theory.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 independently states the assumptions require uniform ellipticity, computes the covariance of the stated coefficient, gives a zero-coordinate counterexample to the ellipticity inequality, and concludes that the claimed verification is false.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 concerns the direction of a viscosity supersolution inequality at a lower test-function contact in Proposition apb1. The gold issue instead concerns an algebraic sign reversal when converting the bound on the constant C_w into the lower comparison shift in ydiffbound. Both involve signs, but they are different mathematical objects, obligations, and operations; ISSUE-003 does not recognize the C_w comparison defect or its propagation to the two-sided estimate.
